subject: Implementation services carveout and private offer anchoring - ask
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearwave.ai>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.example
Cc: Roberto Cruz <roberto@integratech.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Private Offer list price anchoring + implementation services question

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ClearWave is excited by the latency and cost profile you showed on the 4k token workloads. We are preparing procurement and have two quick asks as we assemble the internal SOW and PO: 

- For the AWS Private Offer, do you have guidance on whether the list price for the SKU should reflect only the runtime (compute) component, or can we include implementation (PSA) hours in the same Private Offer line item?
- If services must be separated, we’d like to confirm typical reseller/partner margin splits for implementation (we’re engaging Integratech as the SI). They’ve asked for guidance so we can finalize their statement of work.

Can you point us at a sample flow (or a short note) so we can share with procurement? We need to lock this by EOD next Friday (2027-05-07).

Appreciate it —
Maya
Product & Partnerships
ClearWave AI

Attachment: psa_scope_v1.xlsx (excel, 46 KB)
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.example
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Private Offer list price anchoring + implementation services question

Maya — thanks for the clear asks and the scope doc. Quick answers below and then a recommended path.

- Marketplace private offers (AWS/GCP/Azure) should NOT include third-party professional services on the same SKU. Cloud marketplaces generally restrict billing to usage/list-priced software SKUs.
- Typical approach: put runtime as the Private Offer SKU (list price anchors there), and bill PSA implementation separately via partner invoice or a separate contract.
- Channel split guidance: for SIs doing end-to-end implementation that also handle some enablement, a common split is to allow the partner to set their services fee independently; for reseller margin on the software list price we often recommend 10–20% pass-through to partners (depending on partner motion). For cross-charge transparency we can support a separate revenue recognition flow.

My recommendation to expedite procurement:
1) Create the AWS Private Offer with the runtime SKU anchored to the list price we discussed (we’ll send proposed list price).
2) Partner signs a standalone SOW for implementation (they invoice ClearWave directly).
3) If ClearWave wants the partner empowered to bill a combined invoice, include a reference in the SOW and attach the partner invoice template.

I attached a short note and example PO draft to illustrate. If this matches your procurement team's preference, Ben can help draft the AWS template for the private offer.

Next step: can we get a final decision by EOD Friday so we can spin the PO and partner SOW?

—Nikhil
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal_v3.pdf (pdf, 128 KB)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearwave.ai>, nikhil_sharma@redwood.example
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 14:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Private Offer list price anchoring + implementation services question

Maya — adding a couple practical constraints from deal ops / marketplace listing side: 

- Marketplaces (esp. AWS) do not allow a bundled SKU that mixes managed runtime + professional services. The software SKU must map to our listing; services go separate.
- For commercial modeling, if Integratech expects a margin off software, a 60/40 split (partner/customer/revenue share variations) is common when partners do heavy implementation and bring the ARR. We can be flexible but need to track partner-commission vs. reseller revenue for payouts.

If ClearWave wants the partner to own implementation margins, we can allow Integratech to charge 80% of their services list rate and return 20% to the reseller pool, but that is more of a negotiated partner compensation (not recommended for standard deals).

Operational ask: if you want us to anchor the private offer at a lower list price to effectively subsidize partner services, we need an internal exception and approval from finance/legal. That will take 48–72 hours.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with procurement + Integratech to align.
From: Roberto Cruz <roberto@integratech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearwave.ai>, nikhil_sharma@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 11:33:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Private Offer list price anchoring + implementation services question

Thanks team — quick note from Integratech's side: the SOW includes custom connectors and on-prem data ingest work which increases our implementation effort. To make the project economics work for us we'd need to capture 75–80% of services revenue (we price their services line at market). We prefer services billed directly to ClearWave but would like visibility into the private offer price so we can model total TCO for the customer.

If Redwood can provide a modest one-time onboarding credit (applied as a credit on the first invoice) or allow a lower list price for the first 6 months, we can accept a 70/30 split in favor of Integratech. Otherwise we'll need to increase their services fee.

Let us know what concessions are possible and we'll update the SOW accordingly.
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.example
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@clearwave.ai>, Roberto Cruz <roberto@integratech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, laura_bennett@redwood.example
Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 10:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Private Offer list price anchoring + implementation services question

Maya / Roberto — appreciate the transparency. Quick decisions: 

- We cannot bundle services into the AWS Private Offer SKU. Confirmed.
- For this engagement Redwood can offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied as a contra-revenue on the customer invoice) up to $18,000 conditional on the PO hitting $240k ARR for the first 12 months. That credit is our way to subsidize initial partner costs without changing marketplace SKU policies.
- Partner margin on services should be negotiated between ClearWave and Integratech; Redwood will not withhold partner services revenue, but we will provide a recommended split and support partner commission tracking (Ben to coordinate the commission template).

Action items: 
1) Maya — confirm whether ClearWave can commit to the $240k ARR PO threshold (this will trigger the $18k onboarding credit).
2) Roberto — please update the SOW to reflect services-only invoicing and send an invoice template; we'll keep Integratech on the commission list but they will invoice ClearWave directly.
3) Ben & Laura — will prepare the AWS Private Offer draft and the partner commission template (expect a 48–72 hour turnaround once we have confirmation).

If all agree, I’ll prepare the PO draft and DocuSign link for signature.

—Nikhil
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
